description: We are a team bridging low-level embedded hardware and responsive web interfaces to tackle astronaut health autonomy. We are building an offline, zero-touch bio-telemetry system that pairs edge wearable sensors with an interactive clinical dashboard for deep-space missions. Our core skills span C/C++ firmware, Bluetooth LE protocol engineering, and modern web UI. Looking for collaborators with interests in UI/UX design, space biology/medicine, or technical storytelling. Join us!
summary:
On deep-space missions like Artemis Mars Transit, communication latency with Earth reaches up to 22+ minutes one-way. Ground flight surgeons cannot conduct real-time emergency triage. Astronaut health telemetry must operate with 100% offline edge autonomy.

Orbita is an autonomous bioastronautics telemetry station that pairs an affordable commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) smartwatch (Amazfit Bip U) with a local offline BLE bridge and an aerospace-grade console—requiring zero internet and zero cloud servers.

Embracing NASA's COTS philosophy (the same principle behind using iPads on the ISS), we reverse-engineered the watch's Huami BLE protocol with a local AES-128 handshake, decoupling it from commercial cloud servers. Orbita extracts continuous optical PPG heart rate, reconstructs beat-to-beat intervals to compute real-time HRV (SDNN), derives a dynamic autonomic stress index, tracks SpO2 drift, and sniffs sleep/wear states.

Crucially, Orbita enables bidirectional emergency dispatch: when local triage detects clinical hazards (e.g., cabin hypoxia or tachycardia), it pushes immediate text alarms and tactile haptic vibration pulses directly to the astronaut’s wrist OLED screen, alongside a 4-channel real-time oscilloscope on the habitat console.

Orbita proves that low-cost COTS hardware paired with intelligent edge software can reliably safeguard astronaut health on long-duration interplanetary missions.
details:
Orbita is an autonomous, 100% offline bioastronautics telemetry platform designed for long-duration deep-space exploration (e.g., Artemis Mars Transit). It pairs an affordable Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) smartwatch (Amazfit Bip U) with a local edge BLE bridge and an aerospace mission console.

The system operates via a local Python BLE daemon (bleak) that performs an offline AES-128 cryptographic challenge-response handshake over GATT characteristic 0x0009, completely decoupling the watch from commercial cloud servers. It extracts continuous 1 Hz optical PPG heart rate (0x2A37), derives beat-to-beat Inter-Beat Intervals (RR) to compute real-time HRV (SDNN), calculates an Autonomic Stress Index (0–100), syncs historical SpO₂ records (0x0004), and sniffs physical wear and sleep states (0x0010).

Crucially, communication is bidirectional: if the triage engine detects clinical anomalies, it dispatches critical text alerts (0x2A46) and haptic vibration alarms (0x2A06) straight to the astronaut's wrist OLED screen, synchronized to Mission Elapsed Time (MET).

2. What benefits does it have?

  • 100% Offline Edge Autonomy: Functions entirely on the local spacecraft network with zero cloud or internet dependency.
  • Mass & Cost Efficiency: Uses a $40 COTS smartwatch instead of multi-thousand-dollar proprietary biomedical rigs.
  • Active Closed-Loop Protection: Vibrates and displays alerts on the astronaut's wrist even during sleep, high-noise vehicular operations, or when away from habitat screens.
  • Zero Synthetic Data: Follows a strict clinical integrity rule where all vitals originate from physical hardware or are explicitly labeled as model estimates.

3. What is the intended impact?

Orbita demonstrates that consumer hardware can be repurposed to deliver mission-grade bioastronautics, democratizing space medicine. Beyond spaceflight, Orbita provides immediate terrestrial impact for isolated environments with zero connectivity: Antarctic research stations, submarines, remote mining operations, and underserved rural clinics.

4. Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used:

  • Hardware: Amazfit Bip U smartwatch (Huami / Zepp OS), macOS/Linux host, secondary ESP32-C3 microcontroller prototype with MAX30102 pulse oximeter.
  • Languages & Stacks: Python 3.11 (BLE GATT reverse-engineering, AES-128 crypto, asyncio, REST/SSE daemon), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+, Web Bluetooth, Web Audio API), HTML5 Canvas (high-framerate sweep oscilloscope), CSS3 design tokens.
  • Libraries & Tools: bleak, cryptography (AES-128 ECB), aiohttp, Pillow (custom 302×320 UIHH watchface binary compiler), Vite, Node.js, and native macOS App wrapper (Orbita.app).

5. How is your project creative?

Rather than simulating fake data or relying on closed manufacturer apps, we reverse-engineered the proprietary Huami BLE protocol, allowing us to:

  1. Unlock continuous 1 Hz optical sampling typically throttled by commercial firmware to save battery.
  2. Programmatically generate a custom 302×320 astronaut watchface (.bin) with live pulse zone meters and flash it Over-The-Air (OTA) via BLE characteristics 0x1531/0x1532.
  3. Reconstruct beat-to-beat intervals from raw packet differentials to derive clinical HRV on hardware that normally hides raw timestamps.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • NASA HRP R.I.D.G.E. Hazards: Designed specifically to counter Distance from Earth (offline autonomy), Altered Gravity (HRV autonomic monitoring), Hostile Closed Environments (continuous SpO₂ hypoxia detection), and Isolation & Confinement (sleep fragmentation tracking).
  • Cognitive Ergonomics: High-contrast, dark-mode aerospace HUD (WCAG AA compliant, JetBrains Mono tabular numerals) built to prevent cognitive fatigue during 24-hour rotations.
  • Mission Reliability: Packaged as an idempotent supervised desktop app (Orbita.app) that monitors background processes and auto-recovers from crashes.
